placementGuidelines: INVASIVE-CAUTION, MANAGEABLE: naturalizes readily near coastal wetlands and marsh edges in Georgia/Florida, so control lateral spread rather than avoiding the plant outright - use physical edging barriers in beds, or contain in pots, and deadhead before seed pods form to prevent self-seeding/rhizome spread. Positives worth keeping in mind: near-continuous purple bloom through the hottest months, strong pollinator/hummingbird nectar value, vigorous drought-tolerant groundcover that fills bare sandy soil fast and outcompetes true weeds. Best used as a contained/edged ornamental rather than a naturalized restoration planting. Adaptable to full sun-part shade; morning sun with afternoon shade protection often gives the most consistent bloom in intense summer heat. Drought-tolerant once established but responds well to consistent moisture; watch for root rot in heavy/poorly-drained soil - amend with coarse sand/perlite or grow in raised beds/containers. If leggy by midsummer, cut back hard to 6-8 inches; rebounds with a fresh bloom flush in 2-3 weeks.
